{{Codex|The favored side-arms of Perrin Sequence executives, these pistols have been modified to improve efficiency and killing potential.}}
The '''Secura Dual Cestra''' is a modified version of the {{Weapon|Dual Cestra}} exclusive to {{Faction|The Perrin Sequence}}, featuring improved damage, [[critical chance]] and [[status chance]], and innate [[Sequence]] effect.  

This weapon can be sold for {{cc|5,000}}.

==Characteristics==
*This weapon deals primarily {{D|Puncture}} damage.
*Innate [[Sequence]] effect.
*Innate {{Pol|Madurai}} and one {{Pol|Naramon}} polarities.

{{Advantages|
*Tied with normal {{Weapon|Dual Cestra}} and {{Weapon|Twin Grakatas}} for the highest magazine size of all secondaries.
*High [[accuracy]].
}}

{{Disadvantages|
*Projectiles have travel time.
*Requires a spool-up of '''5''' shots before achieving optimal [[fire rate]]. Fire rate starts at '''60%''' of the listed value, and increases by '''8%''' per shot.
*High recoil when fully spooled.
*Poor ammo economy.
*Tied with {{Weapon|Dual Cestra}} for the slowest [[reload speed]] of all secondaries.
}}

{{WeaponComparison|Dual Cestra}}

==Acquisition==
*The Secura Dual Cestra can be acquired by reaching the Rank of '''Partner''' with {{Faction|The Perrin Sequence}}, and spending {{sc|100,000}} to purchase. As with all Syndicate Weapons, the Secura Dual Cestra cannot be chosen as the free offering upon ranking up to Partner rank.   
*Syndicate weapons can be also be acquired via [[Trade System|Trading]], but only for unranked copies without [[Forma]] and [[Orokin Catalyst]] installed.
*Players must have a '''Mastery Rank''' of at least 10 to acquire the Secura Dual Cestra, either through trading or through the Syndicates themselves.

==Tips==
*Due to the high recoil of this weapon, {{M|Steady Hands}} is recommended for better accuracy.
**Without Steady Hands, move the reticle downwards while firing to mitigate the recoil.

==Trivia==
*Secura is taken directly from Latin, meaning secure.
*The Secura Dual Cestra is the first item to have the "''Secura''" prefix in its name, with the [[Secura Syandana]] following second and the {{Weapon|Secura Penta}} being third.

==Bugs==
*Currently the Secura Dual Cestra and its counterparts ({{Weapon|Cestra}} and {{Weapon|Dual Cestra}}) cannot increase the damage of {{A|Antimatter Drop}}.

[[Category:Launcher (Primary)]] {{Top|Enemy|Corpus|Corpus|Weapon|Weapons|Weapons}} {{WeaponInfoboxAutomatic}} {{Codex|Ruthless and efficient, just like the free-market.}} The '''Secura Penta''' is {{Faction|The Perrin Sequence}} exclusive version of the {{Weapon|Penta}} grenade launcher, featuring higher [[critical chance]] and [[status chance]], [[fire rate]], and magazine size, but with lower explosion damage. It also comes with an innate [[Sequence]] effect. ==Characteristics== *This weapon deals primarily {{D|Blast}} damage. *Can only have five grenades out at once. **Extra projectiles generated by [[Multishot]] will count towards the limit of five live grenades. *Grenades explode in a '''6''' meter radius upon impacting a surface or enemy. **Initial hit and explosion apply status separately. **Explosion does not need direct line of sight to deal damage and will penetrate walls. *Can use the Penta-exclusive {{M|Tether Grenades}} and {{M|Napalm Grenades}}, as well as the launcher-exclusive {{M|Adhesive Blast}} mods. *Can benefit from {{M|Firestorm}} ({{M|Primed Firestorm|Primed}}) and {{M|Cautious Shot}}. *Innate [[Sequence]] effect. *Innate {{Pol|Naramon}}, {{Pol|Vazarin}}, and {{Pol|Madurai}} polarities. {{Advantages|class=Launcher| *Pinpoint [[accuracy]]. **{{M|Heavy Caliber}}'s accuracy penalty is minimal on this weapon. }} {{Disadvantages|class=Launcher| *Grenades have slow travel time and heavy arcing. *Grenades have a high bouncing capability which makes it hard to stack on a desired spot. **Can bounce off teammates or companions. **This can be countered with the {{M|Adhesive Blast}} mod which will make the grenades stick to any surface. **{{M|Tether Grenades}} counters this, with the additional benefit of keeping a tethered enemy from leaving the blast radius. *Explosion inflicts [[Stagger|self-stagger]]. *Explosion has a [[Enemy Body Parts|headshot]] multiplier of 1x and cannot trigger headshot conditions. *Explosion has linear [[Damage Falloff]] from 100% to 40% from central impact. }} {{WeaponComparison|Penta}} {{WeaponComparison|Carmine Penta|header=n}} ==Acquisition== *The Secura Penta can be acquired by reaching the Rank of '''Partner''' with {{Faction|The Perrin Sequence}}, and spending {{sc|125,000}} to purchase. As with all Syndicate Weapons, the Secura Penta cannot be chosen as the free offering upon ranking up to Partner rank. *Syndicate weapons can also be acquired via [[Trade System|Trading]], but only for unranked copies without [[Forma]] or [[Orokin Catalyst]] installed. *Players must have a [[Mastery Rank]] of at least 12 to acquire the Secura Penta, either through trading or through the Syndicates themselves. ==Notes== *Although the Secura Penta can hold 2 more rounds in its magazine, it can only have five grenades out like the regular Penta. *If fired straight down at a flat piece of terrain, the grenade will bounce straight up until it hits the highest part of its arc, then float very slowly back down. They can still be detonated while floating, making it possible to set up ambushes for ospreys. ==Trivia== *The Secura Penta's magazine becomes visibly larger as magazine capacity is increased. As the model was designed for the Penta's 5 grenades, the default 7 protrude through the bottom of the gun. {{clr}} ==Bugs== *Grenades won't explode if an enemy approaches within 6 meters. They must be manually detonated. ==Media== Syndicateweapons5802.jpg|The Secura Penta as seen on [[Devstream 58]]. penta.jpg|Secura Penta in Codex Secura Penta (1).png|Secura Penta when equipped in the arsenal Secura Penta (2).png| {{SkinGallery}} ==Patch History== {{Scrollbox/Article| {{ver|32}} ;Ammo Changes We understand the power fantasy of these weapons is very popular for some, so our first approach was to keep them powerful, but limit how often they can be used by making changes to ammo pick-up. '''''Ammo Pickup Overrides'''''
The following weapons now have ammo pickup overrides, meaning they gain less from picking up ammo. This mostly applies to AoE weapons, in hopes that players will become more deliberate with their aim to make the most of their Ammo pools. The following lists the specific ammo pick up overrides per weapon category. '''Primary Weapon Ammo Pick Up Overrides''' 5 Ammo per Pick Up: *Secura Penta ;Headshot Damage Changes During playtesting, the ammo changes alone weren’t enough to significantly change things for AoE weapons. So instead of tightening these values to be overly restrictive, we chose to address other factors that make these weapons so strong, such as headshot damage. Our approach here is two-fold, to reduce the impact of headshots for AOE weapons, but to also make precision headshots pack a larger punch overall. *Radial damage no longer gains extra headshot damage or triggers headshot conditions. **This is primarily targeted at the Ignis Wraith - as a “flamethrower” weapon, it’s hard to imagine a blanket of elements being precise enough to target weak points specifically. Explosive projectiles themselves can still land headshots, so there is still a reason to aim with most weapons for maximum damage. {{ver|27.3.16}} *Fixed Secura Penta grenades becoming stuck when Napalm Grenades is equipped, thus rendering the Penta unusable. As reported here: https://forums.warframe.com/topic/1174244-penta-grenades-getting-stuck-causing-the-weapon-to-be-completely-useless/ {{ver|27.2.2}}
Reduced the following AoE weapons Radial Damage Falloff from central impact that were all previously 90%: *Secura Penta: 60% {{ver|27.2}} ;Self Damage Changes: We are getting rid of Self Damage and replacing it with something else: instead of Self Damage, it’s now ‘Stagger’. This change completely removes the chance of killing yourself, and instead now creates scenarios where you will interrupt yourself - or ‘Stagger’ - to varying degrees if you aren’t careful. The degrees of Self-Interrupt start with a small stumble all the way to full knockdown depending on how close you are to the center of explosion. Any Mods referring to Self Damage will be converted to acknowledge Stagger. With this Self-Interrupt system, we have added dozens of new recovery animations that harness a ninja-like recovery experience. By pressing ‘Jump’ at the correct time, you can execute a ninja-skill-based knockdown recovery to ALL in-game knockdowns. This ninja recovery window is indicated by a glowing FX on your Warframe. In the original Dev Workshop, we said:
''As a result of this overall systemic change, Weapons with Stagger will be getting approximately a 20% buff in Damage, with any weapons with AOE receiving a 50% Radial Damage Falloff from central impact.'' This is no longer accurate after continued testing. What we are doing now is: No damage buffs have been added, but any weapons with AOE are receiving ~20% increase in Radius. Additionally, AOE weapons are receiving a 90% Radial Damage Falloff from central impact. This means on the very outer section of the explosion Radius 10% of the Damage will be dealt. Tactics will be deadly - aim true, Tenno. ''Why: Several players brought up the history of the Tonkor and we want to make sure we ship this change in a place that’s conservative in its starting point from a balance perspective. The complete removal of Self Damage does change the pace of destruction with some of the game’s most powerful weapons, so we want to make sure we can iterate upwardly instead of releasing a bonanza of explosions with no other choices.'' {{ver|24.5.5}} *Updated Secura Penta's napalm projectiles when using the Napalm Grenades Mod, so that they better reflect the Penta's stats (higher *Status Effect and Critical Chances). {{ver|22.12}} *[[Status chance]] increased from 10% to 26%. *[[Critical chance]] increased from 10% to 26%. *Damage decreased from 375 to 300. *Ammo capacity decreased from 30 to 28. {{ver|17.3}} *Introduced. }} ==See Also== *{{Weapon|Penta}}, the unmodified version. *{{Weapon|Carmine Penta}}, a special version of the Penta. *{{Weapon|Secura Dual Cestra}}, the secondary weapon associated with The Perrin Sequence. *{{Weapon|Secura Lecta}}, the melee weapon associated with The Perrin Sequence. *{{Faction|The Perrin Sequence}}, the [[Syndicate]] that offers this weapon. *[[Syndicate Weapons]], for other weapons from the Syndicates. {{WeaponNav}} [[de:Secura Penta]] [[es:Penta Secura]] [[Category:Augmented Weapons]] [[Category:Special Weapons]] [[Category:Syndicate Offerings]] [[Category:Syndicate Weapons]] [[uk:Пента-секура]]

==Acquisition==
*May appear as a [[The Steel Path|Steel Path]] [[The Circuit|Circuit]] Tier 1, 3, 4, 6, or 7 reward on a weekly rotational basis.
*May be sold by [[Acrithis]] for 10 {{Resource|Pathos Clamp}}s on a daily rotational basis, requiring [[Drifter/Intrinsics|Drifter Intrinsics]] [[Drifter/Intrinsics/Opportunity|Opportunity]] Rank 9 for the arcanes to appear in her shop.
*May drop from Undercroft portals in the [[Duviri]] Experience while on Steel Path.

==Notes==
*[[Melee Combo|Melee combo]] is consumed every time the player swaps to a secondary with Outburst.
**This includes instances where the buff would be equal to or smaller than the current buff. 
*While the buff is active, swapping to secondary will <u>not</u> override the Outburst buff unless it would provide a higher buff than the active one.
**For example, if the current buff is '''+100%''' (swapping from a 5x combo), the arcane will not override the buff if current combo level is 5x or below when the weapon swap occurs.
**Buffs equal to or smaller than the current buff will be created, but only the largest Outburst buff at any given moment can affect gameplay. 
*Each buff expires after 30 seconds. 
**When a larger buff is created, it overrides both the value and the timer of the current buff. 
**When the buff expires, if a smaller buff exists, it will become active for the remainder of its duration.
***However, the buff is <u>not extended by buffs of the same size</u>, since the expiration of one buff will remove all Outburst buffs of that value. (e.g. Having a 10x buff, and then creating another 15 seconds into the timer will still result in both 10x buffs being removed at the expiration of the first buff's duration.)
**The UI does not reliably show the duration of the buff in situations where multiple buffs exist. Instead, it tracks the timer of the most recent buff, while displaying the value of the largest buff at the time of the most recent buff's creation. 
*The buff does not affect any of the secondary exalted weapons if the arcane is not equipped directly on secondary exalted weapons.
*It is not possible to consume combo count from both a normal and exalted melee simultaneously, only whichever is currently active.
*The {{Weapon|Venka Prime}}'s increased maximum combo count works with this arcane, allowing for a slightly larger buff than is possible with other melee weapons.
*On the other hand, the {{Weapon|Dex Nikana}}'s reduced maximum combo count also works with this arcane, allowing for a slightly weaker buff but much easier to achieve (121 combo count for 220% vs 240 for regular weapons for 240%), especially with initial combo bonus.
*The values are additive with mods like {{M|Pistol Gambit}} and {{M|Target Cracker}}.

== Tips ==
*Works extremely well with melee weapons that have modified [[Melee Combo#Initial_Combo|Initial Combo]].
**{{M|Corrupt Charge}} and especially {{M|Galvanized Reflex}} can increase Initial Combo. 
**[[Incarnon]] melees often have Initial Combo perks, as well has offering mobility buffs when transformed at 6x combo or above. 
*A 12x Initial Combo can be obtained through {{Arcane|Melee Crescendo}}, which is easily stacked by opening enemies to [[Finisher#Ground Finisher|ground finishers]] with [[ragdoll]] grouping from [[Vazarin#Void Snare|Void Snare]], {{A|Airburst}}, {{A|Coil Horizon}}, {{A|Pull}}, etc.
**All daggers can open enemies to a front/back finisher by using the forced proc of a Heavy Attack, in addition to having access to {{M|Covert Lethality}}.
*{{Weapon|Ceramic Dagger|Ceramic Dagger Incarnon}}'s '''Gun and Blade''' perk can stack up to 100x Initial Combo.

== Bugs ==

* Still incorrectly provides the buff, again only for Clients, and seemingly only when using Gunblades. Specifically, {{Weapon|Vastilok}} and {{Weapon|Redeemer Prime}} were used in testing.
* The buff activates when swapping to your secondary in the [[Arsenal]] while the player has an equipped melee weapon with any [[Melee Combo#Initial Combo|initial combo]]. 
* The game only applies and updates the UI for the largest buff value, but still creates smaller value buffs every time a secondary weapon swap occurs.
** For example, if the arcane triggers at 4x while a 10x buff is active, Outburst will still create a buff for the 4x instance, without any UI elements updating. After the 10x buff expires, the next largest buff, the 4x buff, will be active on the weapon until it expires. 
* Due to a UI bug, each time that the player swaps to the Outburst weapon without creating a new buff, the current buff is incorrectly shown to be extended at its current value.
** Ex: 10x buff is active, and a swap slightly later occurs at 4x. The UI will show that the 10x buff (200% value) has been refreshed for the full 30 seconds, even though it has not been refreshed. The UI is now tracking the timer of the 4x buff (80% value), and at the 10x value. At this point the 10x buff is not tracked despite being the active buff, and it will expire earlier than the UI indicates.
